Whole-plant candidates from the index: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt.

Southern_Blight shows plant wilted but still upright. Test image plant is completely lying flat on black mulch. Let me check Bacterial_Wilt.

Southern_Bacterial_Wilt also shows a wilting plant on black plastic mulch - very similar field setting to test image. Let me check one more candidate.

The test image shows a tomato plant **completely collapsed flat** on black plastic mulch with exposed soil in background. No visible fungal structures. The collapse is consistent with advanced bacterial wilt disease. Southern_Bacterial_Wilt matches best: similar field conditions (black plastic mulch, soil background), and the description states it leads to "permanent wilt and plant death" as the terminal stage. Bacterial_Wilt reference showed plants still on supports, while the test plant is fully prostrate.
